source.title: A Quantitative Analysis of the Effect of Batch Normalization on Gradient Descent
source.authors: Yong-Qiang Cai; Qian-Xiao Li; Zuo-Wei Shen

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares batch-normalized and unnormalized gradient descent, reporting first-epoch loss and learning-rate stability on neural-network classification tasks. It uses loss and stability rather than the accuracy measure named in V6.
record.gate_note: The OLS convergence and rate results are regression results, not classification-network training-error results. Figure 4 reports first-epoch loss curves; exact plotted values are not stated in the text. The reported MNIST accuracy-at-first-epoch result in Figure 2 concerns stochastic BNGD across dimensions, not a BN-versus-no-BN comparison.
record.test_reason: Section 4.3 compares training with and without BN in classification networks, measuring first-epoch loss and learning-rate stability. These results bear on V6's training-speed and learning-rate claims, although accuracy gains are not directly compared. This study is not an original source for V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish scaling, convergence, acceleration, and learning-rate-insensitivity properties for OLS, then report qualitative and sometimes quantitative parallels in classification experiments. Arbitrary-weight-learning-rate convergence is conditional on the BN-scale learning rate and is not established empirically for all neural-network configurations.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch-normalized gradient descent with ordinary gradient descent. Neural-network experiments use stochastic gradients and first-epoch loss; the BN parameter can have a separate learning rate.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that BN accelerates convergence more for deeper networks than for one-layer networks, and that BNGD performance is relatively insensitive across a large range of learning rates. The scaling property is affected when weight norms are small because variance regularization becomes significant.

fits_no_version.finding: On OLS, BNGD converges for arbitrary positive weight learning rates when the BN-scale learning rate is in (0,1], with linear convergence under additional conditions and potential acceleration through improved effective conditioning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can improve convergence and learning-rate robustness in ordinary least-squares regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports increasing learning-rate insensitivity with hidden-layer width in stochastic BNGD on MNIST, without a corresponding GD comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The range of learning rates yielding similar early BNGD accuracy can grow with network width.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 36th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 97, 2019)
record.problems: The neural-network comparison is characterized by loss after only the first epoch, before the models have generally converged. Figure 4 values are not stated numerically in the text. The reported comparison does not directly report training classification error or accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: No additional Figure 4 curves were extracted as separate rows: the text describes the shared and separated learning-rate schemes but does not state individual plotted values, and the graph-only curves do not support reconstructing numerical values. Figure 2's MNIST accuracy result is about stochastic BNGD across dimensions, not a BN-versus-GD comparison.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and effects of model size, training duration, or regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation across depth, identity shortcuts, very deep plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Neural-network loss recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below that threshold.
Direct BN-versus-no-BN accuracy gains over training; the named sigmoid, VGG, and Inception configurations; and Fixup residual networks. First-epoch loss does not establish eventual convergence speed.

record.verdict_notes: The record's separated-learning-rate stability finding belongs under V6, rather than fits_no_version. Figure 4's scheme-specific curves are already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not flagged as missing. The supplied text supports qualitative comparisons but does not preserve readable numerical curve values.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including with corrupted or random labels; effects of model size, training duration, early stopping, or regularization.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, and the effects of special initialization or normalization removal.
Comparisons of initialization schemes and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training above the stability limit, curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability behavior in neural networks.
The study reports loss rather than accuracy for the BN-versus-GD comparison; it does not test Inception on ImageNet or Fixup residual networks.
